notes: Sixth sweep (2026-10-23): five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head d04061d with no uncommitted changes; every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, skills_listed 209 and skill_hash 005deae0..., so all runs are graded against the current text.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix. git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only SKILL.md (new paragraphs on dot access and nested chains under the pattern-matching rule, the rewritten In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use) and one sentence on crash reports in references/ex_unit.md. None of the eight rules changed, so all eight are graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard, including: a multi-line from/2 bound to a name is allowed inline, an unnamed from(...) piped into Repo.all() is counted under Write pipelines rather than Build a multi-line argument, a literal returned from a helper is not a call argument, and a separate script that uses MyApp.Blog.Post misses the case check, not the rule.

The caller asked for per-bullet violation counts for the rewritten rules in webhook-parser.md and library-client.md. Those cases are not this one: evals/cases/ecto-phoenix.md has no per-sentence bullets, and neither rewritten rule is in its index list. Checked as other_violations: the multi-clause head rule (sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 publish_post/1 select on published_at: nil and bind only post; every controller show/2 is a single clause) and the dot-access sentence (no body pattern pulls a single field out of a value already held; the {count, nil} = ... matches carry a literal). 0 of 5 runs violate either.

Keep migrations to schema changes: haiku-1 is violated, line 142: execute "UPDATE posts SET published_at = inserted_at" inside the migration's up/0, with a comment (lines 134-136) saying the request asked for it there. The other four add only the column. All four separate backfill scripts now query the "posts" table, so the case check on MyApp.Blog.Post is met by 4 of 5 (2 of 5 in 2026-10-22-d), and missed only by haiku-1, which has no script.

The other seven listed rules: 0 of 5 violated. Every run casts only [:title, :body] and sets user_id on the struct; opus-1, haiku-1 and haiku-2 declare assoc_constraint(:user), sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 foreign_key_constraint(:user_id). All five publish with Repo.transact/2 and a two-step with (sonnet-2 used Ecto.Multi in 2026-10-22-d). Every listing preloads the author (sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 by join), and every controller shows via Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2. Every multi-line map is named first: opus-1 log_attrs (108-112), haiku-1 attrs (115-120), haiku-2 attrs (135-139), sonnet-2 attrs (143-147); sonnet-1 builds its map in audit_log_attrs/1. Directive order is clean in every module.

other_violations follow the 2026-10-22-d standard (a pipeline that starts with a call, two transformations on one line, single-step pipes, a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc; missing docs on schema modules, migrations and controllers do not count). Found: haiku-1 from(...) |> Repo.all() at lines 78-83, and haiku-2 two pipes on one with line, line 127. Assumption and reason comments (opus-1 105-106, haiku-1 4-10 and 134-136, haiku-2 1-7, sonnet-1 80-81, sonnet-2 140-141) say what the code cannot show and are not counted.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain mix format adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As before, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls in locals_without_parens: opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 pass; sonnet-2 fails on line 26, a 103-character query = from(...) that the formatter wraps after `=`. sonnet-2 ran no command, so that line is recorded under Before you finish (step 1, run mix format on the changed file).
